text:
Zayne Parekh is 20 and the Calgary conversation has already moved from whether he can play to how good he is. The Win Column asked if he is already a top defenseman in the NHL, and Sportsnaut wrote that he is challenging one of hockey's oldest positional rules. He has ten points in 24 games, five on the power play, at 18 and a half minutes a night.

Our numbers are encouraging without being breathless. Calgary takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), six points better than without him, on a team at 46% overall. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 86th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists. For context, of the 25 defensemen picked seventh to 11th from 2005 to 2024 with four-plus seasons, 19 reached 200 games, and the median first full season was 0.25 points a game. He scored 33 goals as an OHL defenseman in his draft year. Our range has him around 31 points.
